interest: This file provides a fascinating granular view into the post-World War II untangling of frozen Axis assets, wartime banking records, and foreign creditor claims against Japanese financial institutions in the United States and occupied Asia. It highlights the complex jurisdictional web involving the Department of State, the Department of Justice's Office of Alien Property, the New York State Superintendent of Banks, SCAP's Civil Property Custodian in occupied Tokyo, and the Chinese Nationalist liquidation authorities in Shanghai. The subfiles illustrate the legal hurdles faced by non-U.S. claimants under Public Law 671 and strict statutory filing deadlines, the destruction and loss of wartime branch records, and even the micro-historical personal remnants of Japanese overseas bank managers in the custody of the U.S. government.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.51611) spans September 1947 to May 1949 and documents the investigation and resolution of financial claims and assets connected to U.S. and overseas branches of Japanese banks following World War II. The primary matter concerns efforts by the Royal Siamese Embassy and the Department of State to trace a pre-war credit of $6,455.00 belonging to the Siamese trading firm Pisal Panite Trading Company, transmitted in 1941 through Banca Commerciale Italiana and the New York and Osaka offices of Sumitomo Bank, which was frozen under wartime orders and subsequently barred by statutory liquidation filing deadlines and citizenship restrictions under Public Law 671. A second set of despatches from the U.S. Embassy in Nanking investigates an American citizen's $60,387.73 claim against the Yokohama Specie Bank and the puppet Hua Hsing Commercial Bank in Shanghai for a 1941 lubricating oil shipment to Maruzen Sekiyu Kabushiki Kaisha. Finally, a 1949 memorandum from the Division of Protective Services records the discovery of one dollar and a one-yen note among the San Francisco branch records of Mitsuhiro Motoyoshi, former manager of the Yokohama Specie Bank.

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting reports from the Japanese Ministry of Finance and the Sumitomo Bank regarding credits of the Siamese firm Pisal Panite.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (Counselor of Mission)
subfiles.summary: The Counselor of Mission at Tokyo transmits findings regarding an inquiry from the State Department into credits held by the Siamese firm Pisal Panite in the Sumitomo Bank of Osaka. The matter had been referred through SCAP's Civil Property Custodian to the Japanese Ministry of Finance, which procured a report from the bank. Accompanying reports from the Japanese Finance Ministry and the Sumitomo Bank are enclosed for the Department of State's information.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1276 from USPOLAD Tokyo on Credits of Pisal Panite in Sumitomo Bank

subfiles.about: Covering memorandum transmitting Sumitomo Bank's report on the account of Pisal Panite Trading Company.
subfiles.from: S. Miyakawa for Takeshi Watanabe, Director of Liaison Office, Ministry of Finance, Japanese Government
subfiles.summary: The Ministry of Finance of the Japanese Government replies to SCAP's Civil Property Custodian memorandum of July 25, 1947 regarding the account of Pisal Panite Trading Company. Following an investigation, the Ministry confirms that Sumitomo Bank has no outstanding balance for the Siamese firm in Japan. The bank's formal report to the Chief of the Administration Bureau is submitted as an attachment.
subfiles.title: Memorandum L.O. 2818 (AD/FP) from Japanese Ministry of Finance to Civil Property Custodian, GHQ

subfiles.about: Detailed report on the historical handling and freezing of Pisal Panite Trading Company funds.
subfiles.from: Ken'ichiro Mizugaki, Manager, Liaison Department, The Sumitomo Bank, Limited, Osaka
subfiles.summary: The Sumitomo Bank reports that in March 1941 its New York Agency received $6,455.00 from Banca Commerciale Italiana by order of 'Bankasia' for the account of Pisal Panite Trading Co. Lacking instructions from Japan, the New York Agency placed the funds into a Head Office account before the money was frozen by U.S. government wartime orders. Osaka records confirm the funds were never transferred to Japan, suggesting that further trace of the assets must be sought among New York agency records held by the U.S. liquidator.
subfiles.title: Report from Sumitomo Bank to Administration Bureau, Japanese Ministry of Finance
subfiles.to: H. Naganuma, Chief, Administration Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Department of State note transmitting Siamese Embassy and Sumitomo Bank correspondence to the Office of Alien Property.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the Attorney General and the Office of Alien Property copies of letters from the Siamese Ambassador and the Sumitomo Bank of Osaka concerning the account of Pisal Panite Trading Company. The transmittal notes that the Siamese Embassy is being informed of the Sumitomo Bank's response and requests that the Office of Alien Property examine its own records and supply any pertinent information.
subfiles.title: Transmittal Note from Secretary of State to Attorney General regarding Pisal Panite Account
subfiles.to: Attorney General / Office of Alien Property, Department of Justice

subfiles.about: Diplomatic note informing the Siamese Ambassador of the findings of the Sumitomo Bank in Osaka.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State informs the Ambassador of Siam of the results of inquiries conducted through the U.S. Political Adviser in Japan regarding the Pisal Panite Trading Company account. The note quotes extensively from the Sumitomo Bank's statement explaining that the $6,455.00 received in New York in March 1941 was frozen by U.S. orders and never remitted to Japan. The State Department adds that it has requested the Office of Alien Property to search its records for further traces of the account.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to the Ambassador of Siam

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on Chinese government investigations into a wartime commercial claim against the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Nanking (J. Leighton Stuart / C. H. Boehringer)
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy in Nanking forwards supplementary information to the Department of State for transmission to the Department of Justice concerning a claim by an American citizen for $60,387.73. The claim arises from a 1941 shipment of lubricating oil to Maruzen Sekiyu Kabushiki Kaisha financed through the Yokohama Specie Bank and guaranteed by the puppet Hua Hsing Commercial Bank in Shanghai. Enclosed diplomatic notes show that the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs instructed the Central Bank of China to examine the liquidated bank's books.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1074 from American Embassy Nanking on Claim against Yokohama Specie Bank

subfiles.about: Embassy note requesting Chinese authorities to inspect the account books of the Hua Hsing Commercial Bank.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Nanking
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy requests that Chinese liquidators inspecting the records of the puppet Hua Hsing Commercial Bank verify whether any record exists of a letter of credit for an American firm's 1941 oil shipment to Maruzen Sekiyu Kabushiki Kaisha in Shanghai. The note expresses appreciation for prior investigative efforts and requests continued cooperation during the bank's liquidation.
subfiles.title: Note No. 1031 from American Embassy Nanking to Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China
subfiles.to: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of China

subfiles.about: Preliminary reply from the Chinese Foreign Ministry regarding the inspection of Hua Hsing Bank records.
subfiles.from: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of China
subfiles.summary: The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs acknowledges the American Embassy's request regarding the bill of exchange guaranteed by the puppet Hua Hsing Bank through the Yokohama Specie Bank. The Ministry informs the Embassy that the Ministry of Finance has cabled instructions to the Central Bank of China to investigate the records during liquidation and submit a report. A full reply will be provided once the Central Bank concludes its investigation.
subfiles.title: Note No. Tung-36/22742 from Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs to American Embassy Nanking

subfiles.about: Diplomatic note acknowledging State Department information on the Sumitomo Bank account.
subfiles.from: The Siamese Ambassador, Royal Siamese Embassy, Washington
subfiles.summary: The Siamese Ambassador acknowledges receipt of the State Department's note of October 23, 1947 regarding the funds of Pisal Panite Trading Company. The Embassy notes that the funds were never transferred to Japan according to Sumitomo Bank records and expresses appreciation for the State Department's initiative in requesting a search of Office of Alien Property records.
subfiles.title: Note No. 1754/2490 from Siamese Ambassador to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Department file copy of the diplomatic note sent to the Siamese Ambassador on October 23, 1947.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: This file copy reproduces the State Department's third-person note to the Siamese Ambassador transmitting the Sumitomo Bank's report. It recites the transfer history of the $6,455.00 through Banca Commerciale Italiana in New York and its freezing prior to any transfer to Japan, while confirming that an inquiry has been sent to the Office of Alien Property.
subfiles.title: File Copy of Note from Secretary of State to Siamese Ambassador

subfiles.about: Reading and file copy of the transmittal note from the State Department to the Attorney General.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: This document is the official reading file copy of the Secretary of State's transmittal note to the Attorney General and the Office of Alien Property. It forwards copies of communications from the Siamese Ambassador and the Sumitomo Bank regarding the Pisal Panite account and requests any pertinent information held by the Department of Justice.
subfiles.title: Reading Copy of Transmittal Note from Secretary of State to Attorney General
subfiles.to: Attorney General / Office of Alien Property, Department of Justice

subfiles.about: Preliminary response from the Office of Alien Property stating that Washington records show no trace of the account.
subfiles.from: David L. Bazelon, Assistant Attorney General, Director, Office of Alien Property
subfiles.summary: Assistant Attorney General David L. Bazelon responds to the State Department's October 23 inquiry concerning the Pisal Panite Trading Company account. He states that Washington headquarters records contain no information on the account and notes that an inquiry has been directed to the Office of Alien Property's New York Office. A further report will be provided once New York responds.
subfiles.title: Letter from David L. Bazelon (OAP) to Abbot L. Moffat (State Department)
subfiles.to: Abbot L. Moffat, Chief, Division of Southeast Asian Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting final findings of Chinese liquidation authorities regarding the claim against the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Nanking (J. Leighton Stuart / C. H. Boehringer)
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy in Nanking transmits a translation of a note from the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs reporting that examinations of the books of both the Hua Hsing Commercial Bank and the Yokohama Specie Bank in Shanghai revealed no record of the American citizen's $60,387.73 claim. The Chinese authorities suggest that the claimant pursue inquiries directly with the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1150 from American Embassy Nanking on Yokohama Specie Bank Claim

subfiles.about: Note from the Chinese Foreign Ministry explaining why no record exists in Hua Hsing Bank books.
subfiles.from: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of China
subfiles.summary: The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs informs the American Embassy that the liquidator of the puppet Hua Hsing Bank found no record of the letter of credit because the bank possessed no direct foreign banking connections and handled foreign exchange exclusively through the Yokohama Specie Bank. Furthermore, an inspection by the Bank of China of the Yokohama Specie Bank Shanghai branch's guaranteed liabilities showed no trace of the transaction. The Ministry advises that the American claimant apply directly to the Yokohama Specie Bank in Japan.
subfiles.title: Note No. Tung-36/26315 from Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs to American Embassy Nanking

subfiles.about: Internal routing slip transferring Alien Property correspondence to the Division of Financial Affairs.
subfiles.from: Miss Coates, Division of Southeast Asian Affairs (SEA), Department of State
subfiles.summary: Miss Coates of the Division of Southeast Asian Affairs forwards the substantive report from the Office of Alien Property to Mr. Doherty in the Division of Financial Affairs for departmental action, referencing a preceding telephone discussion.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Miss Coates (SEA) to Mr. Doherty (FN)
subfiles.to: Edward W. Doherty, Division of Financial Affairs (FN), Department of State

subfiles.about: Substantive legal and factual report on the status and bar of Pisal Panite's claim.
subfiles.from: David L. Bazelon, Assistant Attorney General, Director, Office of Alien Property
subfiles.summary: Assistant Attorney General Bazelon provides an exhaustive review of the Pisal Panite account based on records of Banca Commerciale Italiana, confirming that $6,455.00 was cabled to Osaka in 1941, but that an attempted repayment was rejected by Torino. He explains that Pisal Panite is legally barred from filing claims both with the New York State Superintendent of Banks due to the expiration of the 1942 statutory deadline (subject to pending litigation over wartime communications failures) and with the Office of Alien Property because Public Law 671 restricts debt claims to U.S. citizens and continuous residents. A copy of Public Law 671 is enclosed for transmittal to the Siamese government.
subfiles.title: Letter from David L. Bazelon (OAP) to Abbot L. Moffat (State) regarding Legal Status of Pisal Panite Claim
subfiles.to: Abbot L. Moffat, Chief, Division of Southeast Asian Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Diplomatic note conveying the Department of Justice's comprehensive legal analysis to the Siamese Embassy.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits the detailed findings of the Office of Alien Property to the Siamese Ambassador, quoting Bazelon's letter in full. The note details the banking transaction history, explains that claims are currently barred under New York liquidation law and Public Law 671, points out pending New York court litigation concerning wartime bar dates, and encloses a copy of Public Law 671.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to the Ambassador of Siam Transmitting OAP Findings

subfiles.about: Legal adviser's routing slip noting the status of New York litigation on the bar date.
subfiles.from: S. Mamer, Office of the Legal Adviser, Department of State
subfiles.summary: A handwritten and typed routing note from the Legal Adviser's office advises Mr. Doherty that the Siamese Embassy's follow-up request can be ignored. It notes advice from Gross of the Office of Alien Property indicating that no judicial decision has been reached regarding the New York liquidation bar date, any ruling will certainly be appealed, and Siamese representatives should maintain direct contact with New York banking authorities.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Legal Adviser's Office (S. Mamer) to Edward W. Doherty (FN)
subfiles.to: Edward W. Doherty, Division of Financial Affairs (FN), Department of State

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum proposing to ignore the Siamese Embassy's request for ongoing litigation updates.
subfiles.from: Edward W. Doherty, Division of Financial Affairs (FN), Department of State
subfiles.summary: Edward W. Doherty recommends that the Department of State decline to monitor and report on problematical future legal proceedings in New York courts as requested by the Siamese Embassy. He argues that all available information has already been supplied and that the Department should take no further action unless the Siamese government repeats its request. A marginal note queries whether the legal division might notify them when appropriate.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Edward W. Doherty (FN) on Siamese Embassy Request
subfiles.to: Office of Financial and Development Policy (OE) / Legal Adviser (L/E)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic note thanking State for its assistance and requesting notification of the New York court decision.
subfiles.from: The Siamese Ambassador, Royal Siamese Embassy, Washington
subfiles.summary: The Siamese Ambassador acknowledges the State Department's note of March 16, 1948 and conveys deep appreciation for the assistance provided by the State Department and the Office of Alien Property. Noting that Pisal Panite's sole hope for filing a claim rests on a favorable ruling in the pending New York court test of wartime bar dates, the Ambassador requests that the Embassy be notified when a decision is rendered.
subfiles.title: Note No. 444/2491 from Siamese Ambassador to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum reporting the discovery of currency among files of the Yokohama Specie Bank San Francisco branch.
subfiles.from: K. Okami, Division of Protective Services (DS), Department of State
subfiles.summary: K. Okami reports discovering a small yellow envelope containing one U.S. dollar bill and a one-yen Japanese paper note among the San Francisco branch records and personal snapshots of Mitsuhiro Motoyoshi, former manager of the Yokohama Specie Bank. The memorandum notes that the Japanese yen note was returned to the chancery folder (S.F. 4-2) of the former Japanese Embassy, while the one-dollar bill is enclosed for departmental disposition.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from K. Okami to Walter Chappell regarding Cash Found in San Francisco Files
subfiles.to: Walter Chappell, Division of Protective Services (DS), Department of State
